README: theoretical and vendor CCD quantum-efficiency measurements are in QE. Northernmost and southernmost eight CCDs have a single-layer AR coating; the inner eight have a multi-layer coating. No headers. Full single-layer file: 230 rows, first column 301.65..1098.19, second 0.000311..0.91512. Full multi2 file: 180 rows, first column 301.68..1038.49, second 0.01351..0.92567. QE/e2v_test_data.xlsx (51114 bytes) was listed and not opened.

u.dat is 2291 bytes and has a header for five columns: wavelength; sensitivity through airmass 1.3 for a point source; through airmass 1.3 for an extended source; through airmass 0.0 for an extended source; atmospheric extinction through 1.0 airmasses. First data row 2980 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0727. The file does not spell the wavelength unit. Page column list: (1) wavelength; (2) on-the-sky sensitivity through 1.3 airmasses at APO for a point source, which defines the survey photometric system; (3) the same for very large sources, different from column 2 only for ri because of infrared scattering; (4) the response of the third column with no atmosphere; (5) assumed atmospheric transparency at one airmass at Apache Point. Page also shows the survey curves as including 1.3 airmasses at APO. g.dat, r.dat, i.dat, z.dat are linked and were not opened.

Opened table title '2MASS J-BAND FILTER TRANSMISSION'. Columns n, xlam, yval. First row 1 1.050 0.0000. No unit word. Parent page item 6 is J filter transmission. H and Ks filter tables are tbl8 and tbl10 and were not opened.

Opened J table title '2MASS J-band Relative Spectral Response Curve'. No column header. First rows 1.062 0. and 1.066 4.07068E-04. Page: Cohen et al. (2003 AJ 126 1090) determined photon-counting RSRs by combining the transmission and QE curves in section III.1.b1, peak-normalized, including atmospheric transmission modeled by PLEXUS. Quoted text: the curves are designed to be integrated directly over stellar spectra in F_lambda form; the QE-based component was converted to yield photon-counting RSRs by multiplying by wavelength and renormalized, as described by Bessel (2000). J values in Table 1 correspond to about 5.0 mm of water vapour and use PLEXUS rather than the simpler ATRAN figures. H and Ks RSR tables are sec6_4a.tbl2.html and tbl3.html and were not opened. Wavelength unit is not in the J table.
